v19.title: UIO V19 — how the car park is built today (distributor level)
engine: History (roughly 1990–2025): trucks registered each year × survival curve = trucks still in service. Truck curve ≈ 9.9-year life (~10.2% scrap/year). Pickup curve ≈ 8.1-year life (~12.3% scrap/year).
Forecast (2026–2030) on most Overview rows: flat rule UIO × 0.97 + new registrations (3% scrap). That is the known defect V20 replaces.
Grand Total (sheet 1 row 2) is a SUMPRODUCT. MIDI toggle B4: policy default Exclude MIDI for ISZE KPIs; live file has often been left on Include — check before quoting.

rules: Separate sheet: 4. ITUK UIO Projection — not the flat 3% rule.
2008–2024: SMMT / DVLA registered car park (actual).
2025–2030: cohort × model survival (N35/N75 from ITUK attrition pack; N50/55 and N62/65 use N75 curve; F-series uses IML CV Advanced Economy).
New regs: Niguri FY25/26–FY27/28, then flat 2,446/year.
Owner-operator floor: pre-2008 and 2008–2010 cohorts held at 90% survival / 10% scrap every forecast year (V15/V17 fix).
Sheet 1 rows 22 and 24 are live-linked to Sheet 4 Section C. Leave alone in V20.
Hardcoded on Overview — not linked to Sheet 4.
V19 uses the same broken 3% scrap + regs roll-forward from 2026F.
2025E 47,783 is kept (direction matches IMIT). V19 2026F 49,280 is wrong-direction and must not be used for GPS.
V20 locks CY2026F at 44,926 (see V20 chapter).
June 2026: replaced estimates with government / dealer registration data (SIMI-class for Ireland).
History rebuilt correctly with survival curves — fleet levels went down vs prior estimates (that drop was correct).
Forecast columns still inherit the network-wide 3% scrap bug until V20.
V19-1 / V19-2 Changelog: UTI parc rebuilt on UTI shipment file (2024 10,049 → 2025 10,336 → 2026 10,760 → 2027 10,972).
UMI is a separate Israel distributor — never blend UTI + UMI into one 'Israel' for IDS or GPS.
V20: government Ministry of Transport register shows UTI row still ~25% low every year — rebuild required.
Separate row set from UTI. IDS Israel country pack is UMI network only.
Do not average or blend with UTI for any IDS-linked or single 'Israel' headline.
IML calculation.xlsx backbone: shipment × survival convolution (Hasegawa-style) for history.
From V18 (June 2026): forecast driven by IMIT LCV study + ISZE CV mid-term plan registrations, still compounded with the 3% scrap rule on Overview forecast columns.
Belgium, Cyprus, Malta, Greece: no real registration history — IML / scrap-adjusted estimates only (low confidence; VIN check implies impossible 0.3–3% scrap).
Germany: history for 2019–2024 partly fabricated by running 3% backwards from a 2025 point — treat as indicative.

v20.title: UIO V20 — specification and new evidence (not a finished workbook yet)
v20.status: Draft in 06_uio/_CURRENT/V20_SPEC.md (27 Jul 2026, amended 30 Jul). Nothing built into the live xlsx yet except the locked IUK LCV decision for planning.

problems.name: Forecast scrap rate
problems.fix: Delete flat 3% rule for 2026–2030. Use the same survival curves as history on every Overview row except ITUK rows 22/24 (already correct) and Israel (full rebuild).
problems.evidence: Grand Total too high by 7.8% (2026) → 37.7% (2030). Ireland 2030 light trucks 1,645 vs 1,382; pickups 3,174 vs 2,527.

problems.name: Pickup direction
problems.fix: Same survival fix — pickups turn down on their own when scrap is real.
problems.evidence: IMIT ISZE pickup regs 16,977 (2024) → 10,845 (2026). V19 pickup fleet still grows ~22.8% to 2030. Steady state at 10,845 × 8.1 yr ≈ 88k vs ~125k on the road.

problems.name: Sales plan vs registrations
problems.fix: Use mid-term plan one-to-one for the level (Jerome 27 Jul). Smooth year-to-year; do not treat each plan year as exact registrations. Split empty medium-duty 'plan only' rows out of Grand Total until a real registration appears.
problems.evidence: Ireland shipments vs SIMI regs 2020–2024: 451 vs 445 (within 1.3%). Single years swing ±50–70. VIN file: zero medium-duty units in 3,238 trucks — Portugal MD plan to 498 by 2030 is fiction.

problems.name: Israel government register
problems.fix: Rebuild UTI rows on Ministry of Transport data (as Ireland was rebuilt). Add 7.6–10 t and 12.1–16 t classes. Add age floor for 15+ year trucks. Do not multiply by 1.25.
problems.evidence: MoT 2026 (30 Jun) 14,019 vs model 10,760 (−23%). Gap ~3.3–3.7k stable across years. Light row 6,101 vs 8,610 (−29%); medium 4,659 vs 5,409 (−14%). 1,680 trucks first registered 1999–2010 still on road.

problems.name: Low-confidence markets
problems.fix: Flag Belgium, Cyprus, Malta, Greece for registration-based rebuild. Do not treat implied 0.3–3% scrap as real.
problems.evidence: VIN × fleet movement only looks plausible for Ireland (13.3%/yr) and Portugal (7.4%/yr).

problems.name: Weight class → target spend per truck (GPS)
problems.fix: Fix VIN GVW decode (NLR=3.5 t not 8.5 t). Split LD car park into N35 vs N75-class where needed. Make GPS mapper able to return the Grafter rate.
problems.evidence: 3,238 VINs look 8.24 t average vs true ~6.08 t. Portugal ~68.5% of N-series is 3.5 t → target spend per truck overstated; GPS % understated ~quarter (indicative).

problems.name: Documentation drift
problems.fix: Rewrite Data Sources / method notes to match June rebuild numbers (Ireland/Portugal descriptions still quote old decay paths).
problems.evidence: Ireland pickups note says 2,648 in 2030 while sheet shows 3,174; Portugal truck note still says 3% decay with no plan.
